evals.prompt:
Meteor 3 app: server crashes on startup with:
[Model] Error registering mixin at index 1 for Issues: Error: [Model] Failed to register array mixin at index 1 for Issues (module: falsy)
Stack shows Model.jsx registerMixins, then Requests.jsx, then Messages/index.js and moduleLink lines. What should I check first and how do I prove it's a circular dependency?
evals.expected_output: Explains Meteor eager eval / cycles, recommends madge on the implicated paths, bundle map check if client/server boundary suspected, and concrete fix patterns (barrel imports, break cycle edge).
expectations: Response recommends running madge (or equivalent) to list cycles
Response ties module: falsy to incomplete module initialization / cycles
Response mentions bundle source-map inspection or the bundled bundle-inspector script for client/server leaks when relevant

evals.prompt: After I added a small helper file under imports/api/notifications, React started throwing Element type is invalid: expected a string or a class/function but got: undefined. Nothing in the helper imports React. meteor reset did not help. Where do I start?
evals.expected_output: Treat as import-order / cycle issue; madge scoped to notifications + consumers; avoid re-export barrels; suggest lazy import or moving shared constants to a leaf module.
expectations: Response recommends dependency/cycle analysis (madge or similar), not only React debugging
Response explains that an unrelated file can reorder evaluation and surface a cycle
Response suggests narrowing the graph to the affected feature folder

evals.prompt: I use per-domain bucket files common.js / client.js / server.js and import them from inside the same domain. I thought ES modules handle cycles. Meteor build sometimes breaks imports when I add files. How do I audit client vs server bundle contents for accidental leaks?
evals.expected_output: Explains Meteor bundling caveat; bucket/barrel pattern risks; run bundle-inspector.js against app.js.map; configure fail-both / fail-server-only regexes; pair with madge.
expectations: Response describes using Meteor build output source maps or the bundle-inspector script
Response warns that in-domain bucket imports amplify cycles
Response mentions madge or depcruise for cycle detection
